chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a group of people who were drinking water with their mouths during the military expedition of Tabuk. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: 'Drink with your hands, for they are the best of your utensils.'

key_terms.أَفْوَاهِهِمْ: Their mouths — drinking directly from a stream or vessel with the mouth, without using hands
key_terms.أَوَانِيكُمْ: Your utensils/vessels — the hands are likened to the best of containers for drinking
key_terms.غَزْوَةِ تَبُوكَ: The Tabuk military expedition (9 AH), the last major campaign led personally by the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about drinking water with your hands in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a prophetic practice from the Tabuk expedition (9 AH), where the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) instructed his companions to drink water using their cupped hands rather than drinking directly with their mouths. This hadith is situated within al-Kafi's chapter on utensils and establishes the human hand as a noble and pure vessel for consuming water. The teaching reflects the Prophet's guidance on dignified and clean conduct during travel and military campaigns.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, for Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> passed by a group of people who were drinking the water by their mouths during the military expedition of Tabuk. So he<sup>saww</sup> said to them: ‘Drink with your hands, for these are the best of your utensils’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ariy from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, once passed by a people who drank water with their mouths during the war of Tabuk.
The Holy Prophet said to them, ‘Drink with your hands; it is the best of your utensils.’”
